ambient_events: A page turns somewhere behind you. When you look, there is nobody there and no book open.
The radiator knocks twice, considers a third, and thinks better of it.
Dust moves through the lamplight in a slow, unbothered spiral.
Somewhere in the shelves, a spine settles with a sound like someone clearing their throat.
description:
Past the last aisle of deeds, the shelving stops being municipal and starts being personal. Somebody has spent years quietly rehousing the things the Hall was never funded to keep: novels, pamphlets, three shelves of translated foreign misery, a run of periodicals nobody has claimed since the Collapse. The labels here are handwritten rather than stamped. There are two armchairs whose stuffing has been repaired more than once, a reading lamp with a burn mark on the shade, and a hand-lettered card taped to the end of the nearest shelf that says TAKE WHAT YOU NEED. BRING IT BACK IF YOU CAN. NO FINES. WE ARE PAST FINES.

A squat brass terminal sits on a side table with a slot for a tablet and a note beside it reading SCAN, DON'T STEAL — IT'S FASTER AND I'LL KNOW.
name: The Lending Library
